domestic.remittances: Re-verified fresh this cycle: FY26 remittances hit an all-time record $41.6bn, +8.6% YoY vs $38.3bn in FY25; June 2026 alone was $3.5bn (+2% YoY but -18.3% MoM off a high May base). GCC supplies ~55% of inflows -- the live Hormuz blockade/kinetic exchange is a forward risk to this channel, not yet visible in the data (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1424957-fy26-remittances-hit-416bn-showing-86-yearly-growth, https://www.dawn.com/news/2014313/remittances-hit-record-416bn-in-fy26)
domestic.current_account: Re-verified fresh this cycle: SBP Governor Jameel Ahmad confirmed FY26 (Jul-Jun, full year) current account expected to close 'slightly in surplus', supported by remittances and services exports despite higher imports -- this is a full-year read one step more current than the prior 11-month ($255mn, Jul-May) print (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429698/remittances-cushion-with-a-catch). This still predates the live Hormuz conflict: Brent is now $87.18 (+4.66% 1d per global.json) after a further overnight escalation -- Trump's 20% Hormuz cargo toll and naval blockade took effect 2026-07-14 4pm ET, Iran fired on a commercial ship and closed the strait over the weekend, and six US-sanctioned supertankers have transited with transponders dark, per fresh CNBC/Bloomberg reporting this cycle (https://www.cnbc.com/2026/07/14/oil-prices-today-brent-wti-hormuz-trump-toll-iran.html, https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-07-14/iran-sneaking-out-tankers-via-hormuz-as-trump-amps-up-threats). Since >80% of Pakistan's crude imports transit Hormuz, the FY26 surplus is a look in the rear-view mirror relative to an intensifying FY27-Q1 import-bill threat.

drivers: Domestic policy anchors re-verified fresh this cycle with new sources, all unchanged and still constructive on their own terms: SBP held the policy rate at 11.5% at the 2026-06-15 MPC (https://www.thenews.pk/story/1420738-sbp-maintains-115-policy-rate-in-final-fy26-review), next MPC 2026-07-27; CPI eased to 11.1% YoY in June 2026 from 11.7% in May, -0.3% MoM (https://www.brecorder.com/news/40428026/pakistan-inflation-hits-111-in-june-2026); IMF combined EFF/RSF program ($4.8bn/SDR 3,348mn disbursed to date) on track, 3rd EFF/2nd RSF reviews completed 2026-05-08 with FY26 primary surplus of 1.6% of GDP in line with targets, 4th review due September 2026 (https://www.imf.org/en/news/articles/2026/05/08/pr-26147-pakistan-imf-completes-3rd-rev-of-extended-arrangement-under-eff-and-2nd-rev-arrang-rsf); SBP reserves $18.47bn as of 2026-07-03 (total liquid reserves $23.99bn), governor projects $20.2bn by December 2026 (https://www.thenews.pk/print/1424970-sbp-forex-reserves-rise-1-9bn-to-18-47bn-as-of-july-3); 6M T-bill cutoff re-confirmed 11.4375% at the 2026-07-08 auction (1M 11.3968%, 3M 11.3978%, 12M 11.4880%), all tenors 31-40bps lower than the prior auction and now below the policy rate (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/08/govt-borrows-rs-2-trillion-from-local-debt-market/); 10Y PIB yield 11.69% as of 2026-07-06, down 1.06pts over the month (https://www.investing.com/rates-bonds/pakistan-10-year-bond-yield)

Idiosyncratic positive amid the selloff: Nishat Group (via DG Khan Cement, Nishat Power, Nishat Chunian Power, Nishat Hotels & Properties) completed a ~PKR66bn acquisition of a 73.9-75.9% controlling stake in Rafhan Maize Products from Ingredion Inc (USA) plus minority holders and a mandatory public offer -- billed as Pakistan's largest private cross-border listed-company M&A ex-privatizations, with Dubai Islamic Bank as foreign-currency lender. This is a genuine vote of confidence in domestic corporate/FDI appetite, but it is a single-name, industrial-diversification story (Nishat conglomerate expanding into food/starch), not a macro regime signal, and does not offset the live conflict shock (https://propakistani.pk/2026/07/14/dada-partners-advises-nishat-group-on-pakistans-largest-private-cross-border-listed-company-acquisition/, https://www.brecorder.com/news/40429832/dada-partners-advises-nishat-group-on-record-cross-border-acquisition)

REGIME CALL: risk-off, held unchanged from the prior two cycles today. Rationale -- (1) the Hormuz conflict remains live and contested (blockade/toll now actually in effect, dark-transponder tankers running the strait, no resolution in sight); (2) Brent/WTI both sitting at fresh multi-week highs per global.json, still elevated intraday; (3) PSX's own tape remains deeply negative (as much as -2.95% intraday, no confirmed recovery to a positive or flat close); (4) desk georisk radar holds at 60/100 moderate with conflict stress maxed; (5) domestic anchors (SBP hold, easing CPI, on-track IMF program, adequate/growing reserves, record remittances, FY26 current-account surplus, easing T-bill/PIB yields) remain genuinely constructive and argue against a capitulation-level panic read, and one large cross-border M&A (Nishat/Rafhan) shows FDI-style confidence persists at the margin -- but none of this offsets a live, unresolved chokepoint conflict hitting Pakistan disproportionately via the oil-import bill. Net: stay risk-off, defensive/beneficiary sectors only, max 2 new setups per desk rules, tight monitoring of existing positions.

favored: E&P (upstream oil & gas -- direct beneficiary of higher realized crude/gas prices, though MARI/OGDC/PPL have still traded red alongside the broad market on index-wide selling; a realized-price economics case, not immunity from the selloff)
banks (quality/defensive, high-rate carry, though also named among today's biggest index drags on broad-based selling -- watch for stabilization before treating as a safe harbor)
fertilizer (domestic-demand defensive, low direct oil-import beta)
avoid: OMCs (inventory/margin and circular-debt risk from volatile, weekly-repriced fuel costs amid a live oil spike)
autos (imported-input cost + weaker consumer demand under fuel/inflation pressure)

cement (energy-intensive, imported coal/fuel cost exposure, named among today's laggards; note DG Khan Cement is a Nishat-group Rafhan acquirer, an idiosyncratic offset worth tracking separately from the sector-wide read)
textiles/exporters (Gulf freight-cost and input-cost exposure amid an active Hormuz blockade)
refineries (crude-cost volatility and margin risk despite the announced $6bn refinery-upgrade fast-track plan, a multi-year structural story, not a near-term offset)
power (named among today's biggest drags, fuel-cost pass-through and circular-debt sensitivity)
